reviews.claim: Implement one transport-free DesignPackageStore that atomically publishes initialized Design packages, preserves bytes across divergent replay, and writes semantic checkpoints on a dedicated history ref without changing product state.
evidence: Atomic publication needs one package-level interrupted-publish observable proving no visible partial package and clean replay.
Package locking must compose existing locked_roots behavior with fail-before-visible-state semantics rather than introduce a public lock abstraction or duplicate lock tests.
Reuse snapshot stable inventory, hashing, staged verification, and publication patterns where adequate instead of creating a parallel implementation.
Creation must define caller-supplied initial intent and design bytes plus an initialized generated-contract destination.

planned_tasks.title: Publish replay-safe Design packages and semantic checkpoints

reviews.claim: Publish a replay-safe active Design package from caller-supplied authored bytes and checkpoint its verified tree on a dedicated package-history ref without changing product state.
evidence: The immutable legacy snapshot entry point cannot create from caller-supplied bytes, rejects all existing destinations, and strips write bits, so it cannot own an active mutable package.
RuntimeTransaction is the matching existing primitive for staged byte publication, locked roots, conflicting-destination detection, and interruption recovery.
Package publication should compose RuntimeTransaction; checkpointing should separately use argument-vector Git plumbing and CAS.

reviews.claim: OUT-001-TASK-001 plans one transport-free DesignPackageStore that publishes replay-safe active Design packages through RuntimeTransaction and checkpoints verified package trees through Git plumbing without changing product state.
evidence: RuntimeTransaction supplies the required staged publication, interruption recovery, locked roots, and immutable destination conflict behavior without duplicate machinery.
The participant contract supports identical byte replay and divergent input or on-disk drift rejection before replacement.
Zero-length generated authority bytes are supported by the existing transaction manifest codec.
Argument-vector Git commit-tree and compare-and-swap update-ref patterns support a dedicated package-history ref without index or worktree mutation.

One focused public-boundary test module covers package replay, byte preservation, unsafe identities, pre-visibility failure recovery, checkpoint identity, and product state preservation without wording or helper tests.

planned_tasks.title: Publish replay-safe Design packages and semantic checkpoints

reviews.claim: DesignPackageStore implements a transport-free active Design package with atomic create and replay through one reused RuntimeTransaction, plus isolated semantic checkpoints on a dedicated CAS Git ref without touching product state.
evidence: create validates safe lowercase-hyphen identities and publishes intent.md, design.md, empty authority.json, and canonical manifest together through existing RuntimeTransaction participants.
Divergent replay and on-disk drift raise DesignPackageConflictError without replacing existing bytes, as proven by the focused public-boundary test.
Injected pre-publication failure leaves no visible package or transaction manifest, and clean replay then succeeds.
checkpoint verifies package bytes before using only hash-object, mktree, commit-tree, for-each-ref, rev-parse, and compare-and-swap update-ref against refs/owlbear/packages/{change_id}.
Focused proof establishes absent initial ref, stable identical replay, child commit for changed content, and unchanged product branch, HEAD, index, status, and worktree bytes.
The exact commit changes only design_package.py, minimal package exports, and one focused test module; independent pytest reports 3 passed, Ruff passes, and editor diagnostics are clean.

reviews.claim: The proposed two-task compiler/admission plan cannot be finalized because the authored Specification does not deterministically carry required schema-v2 known limits or assign ownership or retirement for SemanticUpdate and CompletionSummary after their removal from semantic authority.
evidence: Canonical Design requires schema-v2 known limits, but authored normative fences contain only commitment and outcome blocks; deriving limits from unfenced prose would violate the no-inference boundary.
Current TargetAdmissionCandidate and TargetAdmissionReceipt consume known_limits, so silently omitting them would change accepted behavior without authored authority.

Canonical Design removes SemanticUpdate and CompletionSummary from authority but names no replacement runtime/package record or owning outcome; current Kanban, MCP, Cockpit, agent, and test consumers still depend on those surfaces.

A compiler task that reshapes TargetAuthority is not independently buildable without crossing current projection domains; it can be additive only until the source and relocation decisions are explicit.

Git semantic checkpoint publication and filesystem admission cannot be one atomic transaction; the implementation plan must use idempotent checkpoint-first ordering and receipt-last RuntimeTransaction publication.
Two focused public-boundary test modules remain proportionate once the authority gaps are resolved.
